subject: Discovery recap: observability & evals for Acme Retail
messages:
From: Jordan Hsu <jordan.hsu@acmeretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery follow-up: observability & evals (Acme)

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying points so we can get the SE deep-dive scheduled.

Pain points we surfaced today:
- Lack of visibility into model quality drift across channels (web vs. mobile). We only find regressions after customers flag them.
- No unified dashboards for per-route latency and token-cost breakdowns.
- Evaluation process is manual: golden prompt sets live in a private repo, run weekly but hard to trace changes and regressions back to deploys.
- Rollouts are ad hoc; we want guardrails to prevent noisy failures or quality regressions during canaries.

Current stack (high level):
- In-house model server running on ECS with autoscaling
- Logging to Splunk; limited per-token tracing
- Airflow-based eval pipelines; golden prompts in a private Git repo

Success criteria (what would make this a win for us):
1) Detect and alert on regressions against golden prompts within 24 hours of a deploy.
2) Per-route dashboards showing latency and cost so PMs can make trade-offs.
3) Tracing hooks that let us correlate token-level errors to upstream events (user prompt, model variant, deploy id).

Next steps from Acme:
- Share our current golden prompt set and a small sample of traffic (sanitized). Attached: acme-eval-criteria.xlsx
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with your SEs (we're available Tue/Wed next week afternoon PT).

Thanks,
Jordan
Director, Product — Acme Retail

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Hsu <jordan.hsu@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: observability & evals (Acme)

Jordan — really appreciate the clear summary. This aligns with what we heard on the call. Below is our recap, proposed success criteria, and immediate next steps.

Redwood recap of pain & impact:
- Quality/regression detection: Currently manual; risk of production regressions impacting NPS and conversions.
- Observability gaps: need per-route/token cost + latency breakdowns and a single dashboard for product and infra teams.
- Eval workflow: golden prompts need versioning + automated regression alerts tied to deploys.

Proposed success criteria (suggested):
A) Automated regression alerts that trigger when model outputs for golden prompts degrade beyond a configurable threshold (baseline: 10% drop in accept-rate).
B) Per-route dashboards in Redwood Console within the pilot window (latency, token-cost, top failing prompts).
C) Integration plan for tracing hooks + minimal instrumentation (server-side SDK + request headers) so you can correlate deploy ids to eval results.

What Redwood will deliver for the pilot:
- 1-hour SE instrumentation session (to run through tracing hooks and SDK integration).
- Sandbox dashboard with sample data and a custom golden-prompt monitor.
- Eval playbook (attached) + runbook for regression alerts and rollout guardrails.

Immediate next steps:
1) Jordan: share a sanitized sample of golden prompts + a snapshot of current eval metrics (thanks for the attached file).
2) Redwood (Marissa + Monica + Dylan): schedule SE deep-dive — Tue 3/3 or Wed 3/4, 1–4pm PT windows available.
3) Redwood to send instrumentation checklist and draft dashboard screenshots ahead of the SE call.

Attachments: redwood-evals-playbook.pdf (pilot plan + definitions), link to shared deck: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1xExampleDriveLink/view

Looking forward — I’ll coordinate schedules once you confirm which day works.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Hsu <jordan.hsu@acmeretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: observability & evals (Acme) — SE notes

Jordan — quick technical notes and a short checklist ahead of the SE deep-dive. Thanks for sending the prompt set — it helps a lot.

High-level implementation notes:
- Tracing hooks: we recommend adding two request headers (X-Deploy-Id, X-Route-Id) and forwarding them into Redwood as metadata so the Console and traces can correlate to deploys.
- Golden prompt monitoring: we can run nightly evals against a configurable golden set and surface a "regression score" + example low-scoring outputs.
- Dashboards: per-route panels (p95 latency, median latency, per-token cost, token-count distribution) + a regression alerts panel that maps failing prompts to deploy id.
- Rollout guardrails: canary thresholds (e.g., stop rollout if regression_score > 10% or if error_rate increases by 2x) and automatic rollback hooks via your deployment pipeline (we provide webhook spec).

Instrumentation checklist (attached):
- Add X-Deploy-Id header from your CI/CD at service-side.
- Capture user_route in request metadata (web/mobile/email).
- Forward logs to Redwood tracing by enabling the SDK or via our lightweight forwarder.
- Provide a 24–48h sample of traffic and the golden-prompt repo access (read-only) for initial baseline runs.

Timeline estimate for pilot (assuming access is provided within 3 business days):
- Day 0–2: instrumentation + SDK quick-start
- Day 3–5: baseline evals + dashboard bootstrapping
- Day 6–10: tune alerts + rollout guardrails

I attached a short checklist to make the pre-call work minimal: instrumentation-checklist.md

Happy to cover the webhook spec and dashboard mockups on the call.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com

From: Jordan Hsu <jordan.hsu@acmeretail.com>

Perfect — thanks, Marissa and Dylan. Tue 3/3 at 2pm PT works for us for the SE deep-dive. I’ll share a sanitized prompt set and a 48h traffic dump (S3 link) by EOD tomorrow.

Two quick asks before the call:
1) Can you include a short note on how Redwood handles eval data retention and audit logs? We have security requirements around retention windows and who can access eval outputs.
2) Can you confirm the webhook spec for automatic rollback (we want to align with our deploy tooling team).

We’ll loop in security and deploy leads during the SE call; Priya (cc) will sit in.

Thanks,
Jordan
